faqs.q: Sec. 74-165. - Environmental site assessment based on acquisition or annexation initiated by the city.
faqs.a:
(a)
With regard to any property interest which the city acquires or intends to acquire
               for the purpose of right-of-way or easement, whether acquired, or to be acquired by
               act of eminent domain, negotiated sale and purchase, gift, devise or bequest, dedication,
               or voluntary transfer or trade, the city may have performed a site assessment as may
               be deemed necessary by the city.
(1)
If the city, either through physical examination of the property or because of information
               otherwise brought to its attention concerning the property, believes a condition of
               environmental contamination may exist on the property, then a Phase I assessment may
               be performed at the option of the city. If as a result of the Phase I assessment,
               the city determines the Phase III assessment is necessary, the city may cause to be
               performed a Phase II assessment. If as a result of the Phase II assessment, the city
               determines that a Phase II assessment is necessary, the city may at its option; negotiate
               the cost and timing of a Phase III assessment with the property owner, or terminate
               the acquisition of the property, or perform the Phase III assessment at the city's
               expense, or consummate the acquisition after first taking into account the property's
               condition of environmental contamination.
(2)
Except as to costs allocated to the owner as a result of negotiation concerning a
               Phase III assessment, the city shall pay the cost of site assessments performed pursuant
               to this subsection.
(b)
With regard to any other real property which the city acquires or intends to acquire
               for any public purpose, except as provided in subsection (a) of this section, whether
               acquired, or to be acquired by act of eminent domain; negotiated sale and purchase,
               gift, devise or bequest; or voluntary transfer or trade, the city shall have performed
               such site assessments as are deemed necessary by the city. Any contract for the acquisition
               of real property shall include a provision for a site assessment as an option of the
               city. Any Phase I or Phase II assessment shall be performed prior to the date of closing.
               Any Phase III assessment shall be performed in the manner and at the time mutually
               agreed to between the parties.
(1)
The city shall perform a Phase I assessment on all city initiated acquisitions of
               real property as provided in this subsection. If as a result of the Phase I assessment,
               the city determines that a Phase II assessment is necessary, the city may cause to
               be performed a Phase II assessment. If as a result of the Phase II assessment, the
               city determines that a Phase III assessment is necessary, the city may, at its option,
               negotiate the cost and timing of a Phase III assessment with the property owner, or
               terminate the acquisition of the property, or perform the Phase III assessment at
               the city's expense, or consummate the acquisition after first taking into account
               the property's condition of environmental contamination.
(2)
Except as to costs allocated to the owner as a result of negotiation concerning a
               Phase III assessment, the city shall pay the cost of site assessments performed pursuant
               to this subsection.
(3)
The city may, as a condition of a sale negotiated with any party, require, in form
               approved by the city attorney, a warranty and/or indemnification as to any condition
               of an environmental contamination by hazardous substances found on or affecting the
               property acquired or to be acquired by the city.
(c)
With regard to any city initiated annexation, notwithstanding the existence or absence
               of any possessory or ownership interest by the city in the property to be annexed,
               the city shall cause to be performed a Phase I site assessment on the property within
               the proposed annexation area. Any such Phase I assessment shall be performed prior
               to adoption by city council of any resolution initiating annexation which includes
               the property subject to such assessment.
(1)
If as a result of the Phase I assessment, the city determines that a Phase II assessment
               is necessary, the city may cause to be performed a Phase II assessment. If as a result
               of the Phase II assessment, the city determines that a Phase III assessment is necessary,
               the city may at its option negotiate the cost and timing of any Phase III assessment
               with all or some of the property owners within the annexation area, or terminate the
               annexation proceedings, or cause to be performed Phase III assessments on some or
               all properties within the annexation area at the city's expense, or complete the annexation
               process notwithstanding any condition of environmental contamination by hazardous
               substances.
(2)
Prior to final development, and notwithstanding completion or annexation of environmentally
               contaminated property by the city, the city may require a Phase III assessment to
               be performed on the property previously annexed into the city at the owner's expense
               as a condition of approval by the city of final development. The city may waive such
               assessments under the terms of an annexation agreement.
(3)
Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, the city shall pay the cost
               of the Phase I and Phase II assessments as may be required under this section. The
               city and property owner shall negotiate the payment of costs for Phase III assessments,
               except as provided in subsection (2) of this section.
(4)
No annexation of property by the city, notwithstanding any condition or environmental
               contamination by hazardous substances, or the apparent absence of such contamination,
               shall be deemed a warranty or representation by the city as to the environmental condition
               of such property.
(Code 1981, § 25-84; Ord. No. 3009, § 1, 10-4-1993)
